title: Handle Shopify shipping delays on WhatsApp
excerpt: A practical shipping-delay support process for Shopify: verify parcel facts, send useful WhatsApp updates, assign an owner and follow through.
author: Safwan Adnan
coverImageAlt: A WhatFlow guide illustrates a clear WhatsApp shipping-delay update and the next promised follow-up.

children.text: A useful shipping-delay message tells the customer what you know, what you are checking and when they will hear from you again. It avoids turning a carrier estimate into a delivery guarantee. WhatsApp is particularly useful when the update becomes a conversation about a missing parcel, an address or a time-sensitive order.
The process below works with a small team and a manual tracking check. You can add automation once the underlying source and ownership are reliable. If you are choosing notification channels, our
WhatsApp versus SMS shipping comparison
covers that separate decision.
Key Takeaways
Verify the affected parcel and tracking event before contacting the customer.
Promise a follow-up you control, rather than a delivery date you cannot guarantee.
Give the conversation an owner and keep the resolution separate from sending the update.
Establish what actually happened

Open the order and identify the specific fulfillment, carrier and tracking number involved. A shipping label does not establish that a carrier has collected the parcel. An old scan does not establish that the parcel is lost. A split order can contain both a delivered parcel and one still in transit.
Record these facts before drafting a reply:
Check
Record in the case
Avoid assuming
Affected items
Which parcel contains which products
The whole order is delayed
Last reliable event
Carrier event and its timestamp
No new scan means no movement
Customer expectation
The delivery estimate or promise shown at purchase
Today's website estimate applied to this order
Next dependency
Carrier investigation, warehouse confirmation or customer information
Messaging the buyer resolves the dependency
Next contact
Named owner and a specific follow-up time
Someone else will pick it up
Check the tracking destination itself before sending it. A replacement shipment may have a different link. Shopify describes where customers can
track fulfilled orders

, including the order status page, shipping emails and Shop. If your carrier or fulfillment provider has supplied an explanation, preserve its uncertainty: “The carrier is investigating” is more accurate than “The parcel will arrive tomorrow.”
Choose the correct WhatsApp sending route

Handle shipping updates as service communications tied to the customer's order. Keep product offers and unrelated promotions out of the delay message. Check the customer's permission and the current WhatsApp messaging rules before initiating contact; an order phone number alone is not a universal invitation to message.
With WhatFlow Business API, the relevant messaging route depends on the customer-service window and the applicable approved template. The
WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy

describes a 24-hour service window after the user's last message; outside that window, use an approved message template. It also requires applicable opt-in and honoring opt-out requests. The same constraints matter when a workflow starts the message. Policy and Shopify guidance checked October 27, 2026.

When WhatsApp is unavailable or unsuitable for the customer, continue through an appropriate established support channel. The aim is to keep the buyer informed, rather than force every case into one channel. Our
channel coordination guide
helps prevent duplicate notifications.
Send a clear initial update
Use the customer's context and a concrete next step. The examples here are fictional writing samples to adapt after verifying the facts; they are not automatically approved WhatsApp templates.
Carrier investigation, no new delivery date:

Hi Maya, your order #1042 is taking longer than expected. The carrier's last update was at the sorting facility on Monday. We've asked them to investigate. I'll update you by 3pm tomorrow, even if we're still waiting for their answer. Here's the current tracking link: [verified link]. Sam, customer support.
The promise is an update by a named time. It does not promise a scan or delivery by then.
Only one parcel is delayed:

Hi Maya, the jacket in order #1042 has been delivered, but the belt is travelling separately and its tracking has not updated since Monday. We're checking that parcel with the carrier. I'll contact you by 3pm tomorrow with the next update. The belt's tracking link is [verified link].
The customer needs the item for an event:

Thanks for explaining that you need it for Saturday. I can't confirm that arrival date from the current tracking. I'll check the options our team can offer and reply by 11am tomorrow. I won't arrange a replacement or change your order without confirming the next step with you.
Replace every sample name, time and identifier. If the team cannot meet the stated time, choose one it can maintain.
Keep the conversation and operational task connected

Give one colleague responsibility for the next customer update. Give the investigation its own next action: contact the carrier, check dispatch records or ask a manager to approve a remedy. These responsibilities may belong to different people.

WhatFlow's shared inbox lets the team handle the WhatsApp conversation without inbox seat fees. That makes it easier to include the people needed for the response. It does not mean a carrier investigation, warehouse task or refund happens simply because a message was sent.
A useful handoff is short:

Order #1042, belt parcel only. Carrier investigation requested Tuesday 10am; reference recorded in the order case. Customer needs an update Wednesday by 3pm. No delivery date promised. Alex owns the carrier check; Sam owns the customer reply.
Use your supported internal handoff process for that information. Keep customer addresses, phone numbers and private screenshots out of broad-access team channels. Our
shared inbox ownership guide
covers the day-to-day handover.

fields.alt: An unsaved shipping-delay reply in the WhatFlow canned-response editor

children.text: Actual WhatFlow demo-store reply editor with an illustrative, unsaved shipping-delay draft. No message was sent and the draft was discarded.
Follow up when there is still no news
Send the promised update even if the carrier has not replied. Silence after a missed deadline makes it harder for the customer to trust the next promise.

Hi Maya, the carrier hasn't provided a new scan or an investigation outcome yet. I'm following up with them today. I know this is frustrating. Your case remains open, and I'll contact you again tomorrow by 3pm. If the timing no longer works for you, reply here so we can review the available options under our policy.

Offer only remedies your store can actually provide. Confirm stock, authorization and relevant policy before offering a replacement, refund or delivery upgrade. Record the customer's decision before taking an action that affects the order.
Automate the reliable parts first

Start with reminders and well-defined order events. WhatFlow's Shopify Flow integration can support WhatsApp workflows, but a shipping-exception workflow needs an actual source for the exception. Do not assume Flow or WhatFlow automatically detects every carrier delay.

Before enabling an automated message, identify the event provider, the affected fulfillment, the latest tracking value and how duplicate sends are prevented. Test split shipments and a corrected tracking number. Keep a manual review route for unclear cases. The
Shopify Flow integration guide
explains how to think about connectors and available events.

All available WhatFlow features are included across messaging plans, and the inbox has no seat fees. Messaging allowances and rates vary, with applicable Meta charges separate. Choose the plan for the sending workload; keep the support process clear from the beginning.
Close the loop with the customer

Close the case after the agreed outcome is confirmed or the appropriate follow-up process is complete. A delivered scan may need another check when the customer reports they still cannot find the parcel.

For the next review, count missed follow-ups and repeated contacts about the same case. Look for failures you can fix: an outdated delivery estimate, an incorrect link or an investigation without an owner. Better messages help, but the lasting improvement comes from keeping the commitment behind them.

title: Handle Shopify returns and exchanges on WhatsApp
excerpt: Handle Shopify return and exchange conversations with clear eligibility checks, useful replies, secure handoffs and an accurate distinction between requests and refunds.
author: Safwan Adnan
coverImageAlt: A WhatFlow guide shows the separate stages of a return request, approval, receipt and confirmed resolution.

children.text: WhatsApp can make a return conversation easier for the customer: they can explain the problem and ask a follow-up in the same thread. The actual return, exchange and refund still need to be handled in Shopify or your configured returns system by someone with the appropriate authority.
I would build the process around that distinction. A friendly reply should move the case forward without making an approval, stock or payment promise that the store has not checked. Start with
clear inbox ownership
, then give the team a dependable path from request to resolution.
Key Takeaways
Verify the order, item and applicable policy before promising eligibility.
Treat a return request, approval and refund as separate events.
Keep sensitive information and payment processing out of the chat.
Use WhatFlow for the conversation and your authorized Shopify process for the order action.

fields.alt: An unsaved WhatFlow canned response asks for an order reference before checking return eligibility

children.text: Actual WhatFlow demo-store reply editor with an illustrative, unsaved return-support draft. No customer message was sent and the draft was discarded.
Publish a policy the support team can apply

Give agents the current returns policy and a way to check which terms apply to the customer's purchase. Record the return window, excluded products, item-condition requirements, who pays return shipping and the available resolution options. Product faults or other protected situations may need a different review; do not turn a generic saved reply into a blanket legal conclusion.

Explain the process plainly. Customers need to know where to start, what happens after a request and when an approved refund is actually issued. If the policy allows exchanges only after inspection, avoid a greeting that promises an immediate replacement.
Shopify supports
self-serve return requests

from the order status page when configured. A request still needs the merchant's review. Offer the store's actual self-serve route where available, with WhatsApp as a place to resolve questions rather than forcing a second request into another system.
Ask for the minimum information needed

Identify the order and the affected item through your established verification process. An order number helps find a record; it does not by itself establish that the person messaging owns it. Avoid exposing an address, full order history or other personal details before the appropriate checks.
A first reply might read:

Hi Sara, I can help with that. Which item would you like to return, and is the issue fit, damage or something else? Please use [store's verified order-support route] so we can check the order securely. You don't need to send card details or identification documents here.

This is illustrative copy. Replace the bracketed route with a real, reviewed destination. If a photo is needed to assess damage, say what should be visible and ask the buyer to leave out labels or unrelated personal information. Do not request photos out of habit when the decision does not require them.
Separate each decision in the conversation
Tell the buyer which stage the case has reached. A vague “all sorted” is easy to misunderstand when the parcel has not been returned or a payment has not been processed.
Stage
What to verify
What the agent can accurately say
Request received
Right order and item, request recorded
“We've received your request and will review it.”
Eligibility reviewed
Applicable policy and decision authority
“Your return is approved under the confirmed terms.”
Instructions issued
Actual return destination, label or process
“Please follow these return instructions.”
Return received
Warehouse or returns-system confirmation
“We've received the item; inspection is pending.”
Resolution completed
Actual refund or exchange action
“The refund has been issued,” only after checking it was
Shopify's
return management guidance

describes creating and managing the return, including shipping instructions and applicable exchange or refund details. WhatFlow does not perform those operations merely because the customer requests them in chat. Shopify guidance checked October 27, 2026.
Write an exchange reply that preserves the customer's choice

Confirm the requested variant and check stock before offering an exchange. Include any confirmed price difference or shipping charge before the buyer commits. Do not substitute a different item because it happens to be available.

Thanks, Sara. I've checked your request for the blue medium. It is available at the moment, but it has not been reserved. Your exchange needs approval under our returns process first. I'll confirm the next steps and any cost before you decide whether to proceed.
If the item is unavailable:
The blue medium isn't currently available. I can show you the alternatives, or we can review the return options that apply to your order. I won't change the item without your confirmation.

WhatFlow's live catalog sharing can help an agent show a relevant alternative in the same conversation. That is useful when the customer asks to see another size, style or compatible product. Check the variant and current availability before sending it, and avoid turning a complaint into a pushy sales conversation.
Make the internal handoff actionable

Keep one owner for the customer's next reply, even if a warehouse colleague or manager needs to make the decision. Record the request, checks completed, outstanding decision and next promised contact.
A practical handoff looks like this:

Customer requests size exchange for one shirt. Order verified through the store's support process. Policy review pending with returns lead. No replacement reserved and no refund promised. Jamie will update the customer Thursday by noon.

WhatFlow Business API includes an enterprise-ready inbox without AI and without inbox seat fees. Involving another colleague therefore does not add a seat charge. The team still needs sensible access, a named owner and a clear record of the decision. Our
saved-reply guide
explains how to keep reusable answers accurate without making them sound impersonal.
Follow up without collecting payment details

Use the established Shopify or returns-system process for a balance payment, refund or replacement order. Do not ask the customer to paste card details, verification codes or bank credentials into WhatsApp. For payment questions, direct them to the store's verified checkout or support process.

For an approved refund that has not yet been issued, say exactly that. Once it has been issued, confirm the action and use the payment provider's actual timing guidance. Do not invent a universal “three-day” arrival promise for every payment method or country.
Apply the
WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy

to follow-ups: respect opt-in and opt-out requirements; the service window runs for 24 hours after the user's last message, and messages outside it require an approved template. These examples are writing samples, not approved templates. Policy checked October 27, 2026.
Test the awkward cases before a busy week

Run through a partial return, an unavailable exchange variant and a customer who changes their mind before the return arrives. Ask a colleague to take over using only the recorded handoff. They should know what the store has promised and what remains undecided.

All available WhatFlow features are included across plans, including Free. Messaging allowances and rates vary, and applicable Meta charges are separate. Start with the process your team can maintain, then use
Shopify Flow workflows
where a verified event and supported action genuinely remove repetitive work.
The useful outcome is simple: the customer understands the next step, the team knows who owns it and the order record matches what the conversation says.

title: Use WhatsApp catalog sharing for Shopify support
excerpt: Help Shopify shoppers choose the right product with WhatFlow catalog sharing: check variants, select relevant items and confirm the next purchase step.
author: Safwan Adnan
coverImageAlt: A WhatFlow catalog-support guide connects a customer's product question with a relevant item and a verified purchase step.

children.text: WhatFlow Business API supports catalog sharing today. An agent can show a relevant product inside a WhatsApp conversation while helping the customer choose. The useful starting point is the question: which size, which replacement part or which of two products actually fits the customer's needs?
I would rather send one well-chosen item with an accurate explanation than a large catalog and leave the buyer to start again. Our
product recommendation guide
covers that judgment. This guide focuses on preparing the catalog, sharing the right item and keeping availability and purchase details accurate.
Key Takeaways
Catalog sharing is live in WhatFlow Business API.
Check who manages the connected catalog before changing or syncing products.
Verify the exact variant, current availability and compatibility before recommending it.
A shared product or submitted cart is not proof of payment or a completed Shopify order.
Know which catalog you are using
WhatFlow distinguishes a catalog it manages from an existing catalog already connected to your WhatsApp number. That difference determines where you maintain the products.
For a WhatFlow-managed catalog, the Catalog screen's
Sync catalog

action copies active Shopify products, with an item per variant, and removes deleted products. The available sync settings can also exclude products. Review those settings before changing the catalog's scope: excluded items are removed on the next sync.

For an existing connected catalog, WhatFlow reads it without changing its products. Maintain those items in the system that owns the catalog, such as the Shopify Facebook & Instagram channel, rather than assuming a WhatFlow sync will overwrite it.
The current Catalog screen explicitly says synchronization happens when you click
Sync catalog

. Do not treat the last synchronization as a guarantee of live inventory. Check important price or stock changes at their source before making a promise to the buyer. New or rejected items also need review before you rely on them in support.
These product details were checked against WhatFlow's catalog and product-message implementation on October 27, 2026. Screen wording can change as the product develops.

fields.alt: WhatFlow catalog settings showing manual sync and product scope controls

children.text: Actual WhatFlow demo-store catalog settings, captured October 27, 2026. The catalog has not been synced in this demo. The image shows available controls, not a completed sync or sent product message.
Prepare a small, useful test set

Start with a few products your team regularly discusses. Choose two variants of a familiar item and a compatible accessory. Verify the image, product name, variant, price and destination before anyone uses them in a customer conversation.

Use a test conversation with an authorized colleague. Ask them to open the product and explain what they believe they are selecting. A card that technically sends can still be confusing if several variants share an indistinguishable name or image.
Item to check
Support risk
Useful test
Variant name
Buyer chooses the wrong size or color
Ask the colleague to identify the variant without your help
Product image
Similar products look interchangeable
Compare the image against the actual item being recommended
Price
Old catalog value becomes a sales promise
Compare the displayed amount with the current store source
Availability
A recommendation implies stock is reserved
Check stock and explain whether anything has been reserved
Product suitability
A card is mistaken for compatibility advice
Verify the customer's model or requirement first

Keep a fallback ready. If an item is missing or inaccurate, use a verified storefront product link while the catalog is corrected. Do not send a similar-looking variant just to avoid interrupting the conversation.
Answer the product question before sending the product
Our guide to
pre-purchase WhatsApp questions

explains how to turn recurring questions into better product information. Ask the smallest clarifying question that changes the recommendation. For a replacement part, that might be the product model. For clothing, it could be a measurement from the published size guide. Do not ask for unnecessary personal information.
Consider this fictional exchange:
Customer: Will this strap fit the bag I bought last year?
Agent: Which bag model do you have? The current strap fits the Compact 2, but I need to check the original Compact separately before recommending it.
After confirming compatibility, the agent can share the exact item:
This is the strap listed for your Compact 2. I've selected the black version you asked about. Please check the product details before purchasing; tell me if you want to compare the other color.
If compatibility remains unclear, keep it unclear in the answer. A polished product card does not establish that the item fits.
Choose the smallest useful product message
WhatFlow's product-sharing interface includes
One product
Product list
Carousel
and
Whole catalog
options. Use the format that fits the conversation, rather than the one that shows the most inventory.

For a specific replacement part, one product is usually enough. For a customer comparing two suitable items, a small selection keeps the choice manageable. A whole catalog makes more sense when the customer asks to browse the range.
In the
Send products

interface, select the intended format, choose the relevant catalog item or items and review the accompanying message before sending. The available fields vary by format. For a product list, the heading and sections should help the customer understand the selection, such as “Compatible straps” and “Matching accessories.”
Keep free-form product messages inside the applicable WhatsApp service window. The
WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy
explains that the 24-hour window follows the user's last message and that approved templates are required outside it. Respect opt-in and opt-out requirements as well. Policy checked October 27, 2026.
Explain what happens after a cart arrives

Where enabled, customers can send a catalog cart containing selected items and quantities. Treat that as a purchase request to review. Confirm the intended variants, current availability and the next step in your store's actual order process.

Do not tell the customer they have paid or received a confirmed Shopify order simply because they shared a cart. Use the verified checkout or authorized order-creation process your store supports. Make any final shipping cost, tax or other required charge clear at the appropriate step.
An accurate reply might be:
I've received your selection of two black straps. I'll check availability and confirm the purchase step before you pay. Sending this cart hasn't reserved the items or completed payment.
That small clarification prevents a support conversation from creating a false order confirmation.
Keep useful help easy to hand over

Record the requirement that led to the recommendation, not just the item sent. A colleague should be able to see that the customer wanted a Compact 2 strap in black and that no stock reservation was promised.

WhatFlow combines catalog sharing with an enterprise-ready team inbox, without AI or inbox seat fees. All available features are included across plans, including Free; messaging allowances and rates differ, and applicable Meta charges are separate. The practical advantage is that a product specialist can help with the same customer conversation without adding a seat charge. Follow the
inbox handoff process
so that shared access also produces clear ownership.
Check recommendations after product changes

When the store changes a product, price or variant, review the catalog and any saved answers that mention it. Add a simple check to the team's routine: source updated, appropriate sync completed, customer-facing item reviewed.

The best first rollout is a narrow one: a verified catalog, a few common questions and a team that understands the purchase handoff. Once those work, expand the range. Catalog sharing is most valuable when it helps the buyer make the right decision with less back-and-forth.

faqs.answer: It can help recognition, but meaningful personalization changes the relevance or next step based on accurate customer context.

faqs.answer: The sending process should apply channel preferences and required permissions as well as commercial audience criteria.

author: Safwan Adnan

children.text: Segment WhatsApp campaigns by a customer need that changes the message or next step, using data your store actually maintains. Write the eligibility rule, check missing values and nonmatching examples, then apply permission and opt-out requirements separately. Define exits and campaign priority so relevant groups do not create duplicate or contradictory contact across the customer journey.

Native Shopify customer-segment/audience sync is upcoming in WhatFlow and is not currently available. Select recipients through the supported customer-selection or messaging workflow you use today; do not assume Shopify segments continuously synchronize into the inbox.
Key takeaways
A useful segment changes why the message matters.
Relevance and permission are separate sending conditions.
Test exclusions and overlaps as well as matching customers.

Segmentation is useful when it changes why a message matters. A list divided into arbitrary groups is still a broad campaign if every person receives the same offer for the same reason. Start with a customer need you can support from the data your store actually has.

A buyer of a particular product may need a compatible accessory. Someone who asked a pre-purchase question may need an answer. Those are different relationships and should produce different messages, even if both contacts happen to be recent visitors to the store.

fields.alt: WhatFlow WhatsApp message template configuration in Shopify admin
fields.caption: WhatFlow template editor in the demo store. Sample message data illustrates configuration, not a completed send or measured campaign outcome.

children.text: Use a criterion the team can explain

Write a plain-language audience rule before configuring filters. Include the relevant event, product context and time window. If another colleague cannot tell why someone qualifies, the rule may be too complicated or depend on information that is not consistently maintained.

Keep a distinction between observed behavior and inferred intent. A viewed product can indicate interest, but it does not prove that the person intends to buy it as a gift or needs it urgently. The message should not turn a reasonable hypothesis into an intrusive claim about the customer.
Make data quality part of eligibility

Check missing phone numbers, inconsistent country formats and outdated product mappings. An audience filter can be technically valid while supplying incomplete data to a message. Define what happens when a required value is absent rather than letting a placeholder or wrong product link reach the customer.

Test the rule with representative examples, including people who should not qualify. A positive example alone does not establish that the boundaries work. Look for overlapping groups that could receive several versions of the same campaign on the same day.
Use
campaign boundary checks
to inspect missing values and nonmatching records.
Keep commercial relevance separate from permission

A product recommendation may be relevant and still require the appropriate messaging permission. Build both conditions into the process. Do not assume that an order-related conversation gives the store unrestricted permission to send later promotional campaigns.

WhatsApp templates, the active customer-service window and opt-out handling remain part of the sending decision. WhatFlow can provide the message action and inbox, but selecting an audience does not remove the channel’s requirements or the merchant’s responsibility for the contact.
Use the
WhatsApp Business messaging policy
to check applicable messaging permission and channel requirements; a relevant message still needs the appropriate sending process.
Write different messages only when the reason differs

A useful segment changes the context or next step. A refill audience needs the correct replenishment destination; a compatibility audience needs the relevant specification. Simply inserting a first name into identical broad copy does not make a campaign meaningfully personalized.

Avoid overfilling the message with purchase history. The customer needs enough context to understand the recommendation, not a demonstration of every detail the store can retrieve. Use the smallest amount of accurate information that helps the current decision.
Define exits and avoid audience collisions

A purchase, opt-out or another relevant event should update eligibility where supported data is available. Decide which campaign takes priority when someone matches several groups. Without that rule, carefully defined segments can still create an overwhelming combined contact schedule.

Keep a campaign log that records the audience definition and sending window. This helps support colleagues understand why a message arrived and makes later reporting more reproducible. It also exposes cases where two apps are independently acting on the same customer event.
Include
cross-channel contact coordination
when two valid segments could contact the same buyer.
Evaluate the segment as a hypothesis

Compare relevant responses, purchases, costs and opt-outs under consistent attribution rules. A small group with a high percentage can still be too small for a confident conclusion. Keep counts visible and review whether the campaign reached the intended people in the first place.

WhatFlow’s features are included across Business API plans, with no inbox seat fees, so a small team can begin with a focused audience. Scale the program by improving the reason for each contact, not by multiplying filters that no one can maintain.
Test a segment with explicit counterexamples

Imagine a hypothetical campaign for a replacement filter that fits model A only. The rule might identify buyers of model A in a stated purchase period, provided the required messaging permission is established and supported exclusions are applied. Test a model B buyer, a model A buyer who recently reordered and a record with an unknown model. Each counterexample tests a different boundary; simply finding one matching customer does not establish that the segment is sound.

Write the consequence of missing data before scheduling. An unknown model should not receive a confident compatibility claim as a fallback. Decide which campaign takes priority if the same person also qualifies for a general promotion, then inspect the combined schedule. Compare relevant replies, attributed purchases and opt-outs with raw counts visible. If people mostly ask whether the filter fits, improve the product context or rule rather than creating more segments with nearly identical messages.
Before you put this into practice
Write the audience rule in plain language.
Check missing product context.
Define exits and campaign priority.
